articles.title: ZDI-26-989: TrendAI Apex One Uncontrolled Search Path Element Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
articles.context: An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability
articles.full_text:
Vulnerability Details

This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of TrendAI Apex One server. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the configuration of OpenSSL. The issue results from loading an OpenSSL configuration file from an unsecured location. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM.

Additional Details

TrendAI has issued an update to correct this vulnerability. More details can be found at: https://success.trendmicro.com/en-US/solution/KA-0024778

Disclosure Timeline

2026-06-02 - Vulnerability reported to vendor

2026-11-13 - Coordinated public release of advisory

articles.title: Trend Micro Reports Q3 2026 Results with 9% Net Sales Growth and an 18% Operating Margin
articles.context: TrendAI announced support for the NVIDIA Agent Safety Platform, pairing hardware-level detection on NVIDIA BlueField DPUs with network security and threat intelligence from the...
articles.full_text:
TrendAI™ enterprise net sales grew 12% year over year, and Vision One SaaS ARR grew 46% to US$564 million.

TrendLife™ net sales grew 1% year over year, and Digital Life Protection ARR grew 37% to US$141 million.

TOKYO, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trend Micro Incorporated (TSE: 4704) today reported a 9% year-over-year increase in consolidated net sales for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Company-wide annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached US$1.76 billion. Year-over-year ARR growth accelerated from 3% in Q1 to 5% in Q2 and 6% in Q3.

TrendAI™, the company's enterprise business, grew net sales 12% year over year. Enterprise ARR reached US$1.292 billion, up 8% year over year. On a comparable basis, TrendAI added US$31 million in enterprise ARR in Q3, up from US$21 million in Q2.*

TrendAI Vision One™ delivered strong growth across SaaS, Sovereign and Services. SaaS remained the largest and fastest-growing component, with ARR up 46% to US$564 million. Sovereign ARR grew 15% and Services ARR grew 25% year over year. Existing customers also expanded their use of the platform, with net revenue retention of 119%.

TrendLife™, the consumer business, grew net sales and ARR by 1% year over year. Digital Life Protection ARR rose 37% to US$141 million, representing 30% of TrendLife's US$463 million in ARR.

Enterprise investments begin to show results

In Q2, Trend Micro pointed to its enterprise pipeline as an early sign that its investments would translate into faster ARR growth. In Q3, TrendAI added US$31 million in ARR, compared with US$21 million in Q2. More than 420 strategic managed service providers (MSPs) now sell Vision One, and ARR from MSPs selling the platform grew 155% year over year. Services ARR reached US$88 million, and the number of services customers grew 13%.

"Attackers are using AI to move faster, and that changes when our work as defenders needs to begin. The more we can anticipate how an attack might unfold and prepare protection in advance, the better chance our customers have of keeping their data safe and their operations running," said Eva Chen, co-founder and CEO of Trend Micro. "We see that need reflected in our business. New customers are choosing Vision One, and existing customers are expanding how they use it because they want to act before those threats disrupt their business."

Consolidated financial results

Consolidated net sales were ¥75.3 billion. Operating income was ¥13.2 billion, compared with ¥6.2 billion in Q2 and ¥16.0 billion a year earlier. Operating margin improved from Q2.

Net income attributable to owners of the parent was ¥8.6 billion.

Trend Micro maintained its forecast for the year ending December 31, 2026. The company expects consolidated net sales of ¥301.5 billion, operating income of ¥44.4 billion and net income attributable to owners of the parent of ¥30.7 billion.

Third quarter business highlights

AWS Marketplace sales surpassed US$1 billion. In August, TrendAI surpassed US$1 billion in cumulative global sales through AWS Marketplace, where customers can purchase security using their existing AWS spending commitments. Announcement

Autonomous Vulnerability Remediation entered private preview. In September, TrendAI introduced a Vision One service powered by AESIR that leverages frontier AI models to help security teams identify and remediate exploitable flaws in their source code. Announcement

Security for enterprise AI agents. TrendAI announced support for the NVIDIA Agent Safety Platform, pairing hardware-level detection on NVIDIA BlueField DPUs with network security and threat intelligence from the Zero Day Initiative™. Announcement

Claude Code and Cowork. TrendAI extended its Claude Compliance API integration so security teams can investigate prompts, responses and tool calls from Claude Code and Cowork sessions alongside other security activity in Vision One. Announcement

TrendLife DLP continued growth. As a leader in digital life protection (DLP), TrendLife continued to be recognized for its innovative solutions winning the AI Breakthrough Award for ScamCheck, a cornerstone of its DLP offering. This has helped to propel market adoption of this platform with digital life protection users growing 45% among its installed customer base.

articles.title: TrendAI™ Honors Cybersecurity Excellence Award Winners for Security Leadership
articles.context: 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today announced the recipients...
articles.full_text:
Annual awards recognize customers turning cyber resilience into a competitive advantage

DALLAS, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today announced the recipients of the 2026 TrendAI™ Cybersecurity Excellence Awards. The awards celebrate organizations worldwide for their leadership, innovation, and excellence in cybersecurity.

The winners across the five categories are listed below.

Innovator recognizes organizations introducing new ideas, technologies, or approaches that meaningfully advance cybersecurity

Winners: Sun Chemical; Taiwan Mobile; MITSUI SUMITOMO INSURANCE Agency Service; Qassim University

Visionary honors organizations that are transforming a bold cybersecurity vision into measurable progress

Winners: Pegasystems; SoftBank

Cyber Defender celebrates those demonstrating an exceptional commitment to protecting people, operations, and digital environments

Winners: Keller ISD; Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA); Servico de Salud de las Baleras (IBSalut)

Ambassador distinguishes leaders championing stronger cybersecurity practices across their industries and communities

Winners: Cape Cod Healthcare; Anglicare Victoria; Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board

AI Trailblazer highlights an individual advancing the responsible and effective use of AI in cybersecurity

Winners: Dole Food Company; Pets at Home; International SOS Assistance UK Limited; Rural Servicios Informáticos

Cybersecurity is no longer only about preventing compromise. Organizations that manage it well strengthen customer trust, enable digital transformation, and gain a competitive edge. The 2026 award recipients demonstrate what that looks like in practice.

Rachel Jin, CEO of TrendAI™: "This year's Cybersecurity Excellence Awards represent the next generation of security-first leaders who understand that cyber resilience is not a compliance checkbox, but a competitive advantage. These customers have transformed how they approach risk, turning threat intelligence into innovation, and weaving security into the fabric of business strategy. That's what true excellence looks like."

What the award winners have to say:

Florian Zeeb, Director of Global Information Security, Dole Food Group: "Security needs a seat at the table when AI is adopted, not a review at the end. That is how we make sure AI is used securely and ethically. It only works with the support of management and the teams, and we had both. This recognition is theirs as much as mine. Nobody had all the answers. We learned together with our partners, and we keep learning."

Takashi Hara, Manager, SoftBank: "We are deeply honored to receive the Visionary Award. At SoftBank, we are committed to advancing cybersecurity as a critical foundation for driving social and industrial transformation through cutting-edge technologies, including AI. We understand this recognition reflects our efforts not only to address evolving cyber threats, but also to harness AI safely and responsibly to create new value. Going forward, we will continue to tackle emerging security risks associated with the growing adoption of AI and strengthen our governance frameworks. At the same time, we will advance AI-driven threat detection and analysis, as well as the sophistication of our security operations, with the goal of further enhancing our overall cybersecurity posture."

Liviu Groza, Director Information Security, Cape Cod Healthcare: "This Excellence Award is a reflection on the value Cape Cod Healthcare places on cybersecurity and on TrendAI's ability to meet the demands of operating seemlesly in a space as diverse and sensitive as healthcare. In an increasingly hostile and difficult threat environment, we are able to support the delicate act of healing without undue burden, thanks to organizational backing at all levels and TrendAI's feature rich product suite."

Learn more about this year's awards here.

articles.title: TrendAI™ Brings AI-Driven Security That Runs Entirely Under Customer Control to Sovereign and Private Clouds with NVIDIA Nemotron™ Open Models
articles.context: TrendAI™ runs NVIDIA Nemotron open models entirely inside customer-controlled infrastructure, delivering AI-driven threat detection and policy-based response without security...
articles.full_text:
TrendAI™ runs NVIDIA Nemotron open models entirely inside customer-controlled infrastructure, delivering AI-driven threat detection and policy-based response without security data ever leaving the sovereign boundary.

DALLAS, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today announced it is bringing NVIDIA Nemotron™ open models into TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC), building on its collaboration with NVIDIA. The integration brings AI-assisted security operations into customer-controlled environments, extending capabilities such as guided investigation, security reasoning, and agentic SIEM to organizations with sovereignty, data residency and operational control.

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) is available today, enabling organizations to deploy TrendAI Vision One™ in customer-controlled private cloud, sovereign cloud and on-premises environments. The Nemotron integration extends AI-assisted security operations into these environments while maintaining customer control over security data and deployment.

Why Open Models Matter for SovereigntyHighly regulated organizations need AI-driven security that fits their data-control requirements. Nemotron open models can support these requirements by bringing the model to the data rather than the data to the model. Customers decide where the model runs, which version is deployed, and who can access it, running AI-powered security operations on NVIDIA accelerated computing in their own data centers, sovereign clouds, and restricted-connectivity environments. TrendAI™ collaboration with NVIDIA on OpenShell provides an additional level of security for agents, ensuring organizations have control and visibility of agentic activities.

Who Controls the Intelligence Acting on Your Data?"Sovereignty extends beyond where data resides. Enterprises also need control over where the intelligence acting on that data operates, and how it is governed." says Rachel Jin, CEO, TrendAI™. "Organizations shouldn't have to give up the operational benefits of AI because their security data and operations need to remain within a customer-controlled environment. Our work is about bringing AI-powered security operations to the environments our customers choose to control."

"Open models give organizations the transparency and control to run on their own terms, which is critical for sovereign environments," said John Fanelli, Vice President, Enterprise Software at NVIDIA. "TrendAI's integration of NVIDIA Nemotron models enables enterprises to put their most sensitive data to work, without it ever leaving their control."

Customer Perspective: Sovereignty Without CompromiseTITECH, which delivers sovereign security operations to customers in Oman, is working with TrendAI™ as a design partner on the Nemotron integration ahead of general availability.

"TrendAI Vision One for Sovereign and Private Cloud has provided our local customers in Oman with a trusted foundation for keeping security operations under customer control while complying with country data residency regulations," says TITECH CEO, Mohammed Hassan. "Nemotron-powered capabilities will let us offer advanced threat analysis and AI-assisted security operations to our customers while maintaining data sovereignty and operational control."

The integration supports AI-assisted threat analysis, policy-based response, and guided security operations within customer-controlled environments. These capabilities help organizations improve security operations with AI while maintaining control over where security data and AI processing reside.

Customer Outcome: Security and control from the start"As enterprises apply AI to real-world deployment, security and control must be embedded into the infrastructure from day one," says Business Manager of Security at Bechtle AG, Mathias Schick. "Our customers want to harness the full potential of AI without compromising data sovereignty, security, or operational control. Integrating AI-powered security into sovereign and private-cloud environments is an important step toward enabling secure AI adoption at scale, particularly for organizations with stringent security and compliance requirements."

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) with NVIDIA Nemotron integration supports:

Customer-controlled AI: NVIDIA Nemotron open models deployed and run on customer-controlled infrastructure, with no dependency on external inference services

AI-assisted threat analysis: Reasoning across security signals to identify complex threat patterns, attack chains, and AI-native attack paths

Policy-based threat response: Supporting protective actions through organization-defined policies and security-team controls

Guided security operations: Helping security teams investigate threats and prioritize response activities

Agentic SIEM capabilities: Correlating telemetry and assisting with security reasoning while maintaining team oversight

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) is available today. Visit trendaisecurity.com/platform/sovereign-private-cloud or visit TrendAI™ at NVIDIA GTC Berlin's expo (October 21-22, 2026) to preview these planned capabilities.

Initiative supports nationwide modernization of security measures for individuals and small and medium-sized enterprises, with additional access to TrendAI Vision One™ AI security capabilities and expert technical support provided through partners.

TOKYO, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trend Micro Incorporated (TSE: 4704) today announced plans for the Japan Cyber Resilience Initiative, a major national effort to help Japanese organizations strengthen their cybersecurity, reduce critical exposures and modernize their defenses for the AI era. This initiative is designed to support not only organizations but also individuals.

Japan's cybersecurity challenge is escalating rapidly. According to threat research from TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro, 607 publicly disclosed cybersecurity incidents were recorded during the first nine months of 2026, already exceeding the 594 reported throughout all of 2025*. Furthermore, the growing number of personal data breaches at organizations has exposed sensitive information on a large scale, creating cyber risks not only for enterprises but also for individuals and Japanese society as a whole.

*Cybersecurity incident figures are tallies as of October 9, 2026. Figures may change due to factors such as incidents that are later disclosed retroactively and additional cases being added.

Yet as attacks grow in volume and sophistication, many organizations remain unprepared for the next generation of threats. The growing threat extends beyond large enterprises and critical infrastructure to smaller businesses, suppliers and service providers that form the foundation of Japan's economy.

The program is designed to serve organizations and individuals across Japan, with an initial emphasis on critical infrastructure, major enterprises and the smaller businesses essential to their supply chains. Support will be provided in phases, tailored to organizational needs, eligibility and available resources.

Trend Micro will work closely with its extensive network of channel partners, systems integrators and managed service providers across Japan to extend the initiative's reach. Eligible organizations will receive up to 10 days of professional services free of charge*, delivered through partners to help them access the right cybersecurity expertise and support.

*For details, including requirements for use, please contact us.

Through its enterprise cybersecurity business, TrendAI™, the company proposes to make available up to ¥10 billion in TrendAI Flex licensing credits to help eligible organizations modernize their security environments with TrendAI Vision One™. The initiative also includes plans to mobilize forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) and provide access to managed detection and response (MDR) expertise.

A national challenge demands a national commitment

Japan's senior political leaders have characterized the situation as a cybersecurity emergency.

As a global cybersecurity company headquartered in Japan, Trend Micro has spent decades protecting Japanese businesses while investing extensively in global threat research, vulnerability discovery, threat intelligence and incident response.

"Japan is our home. When the organizations and individuals that power our economy, our infrastructure and our communities face an escalating cybersecurity challenge, we have a responsibility to step forward. No organization should have to face this challenge alone. We are bringing together our technology, our people and our global security expertise to help Japan strengthen its defenses today and prepare for a future in which cyber threats will move faster than ever." said Eva Chen, Trend Micro CEO.

The Japan Cyber Resilience Initiative will provide the following six forms of support to organizations and individuals.

＜For organizations＞

1. Up to ¥10 billion to accelerate cybersecurity modernization

Trend Micro proposes an aggregate allocation of up to ¥10 billion in TrendAI Flex licensing credits to help eligible organizations adopt and expand protection through the TrendAI Vision One™ platform designed to help customers modernize their existing security environments, strengthen protection across critical systems. Through TrendAI Flex Unlimited, customers will also be able to access additional TrendAI Vision One™ capabilities, including AI security innovations.

The initiative will also help existing customers, working with their trusted channel partners where appropriate, build on their current security investments and transition toward modern, AI-era defenses without unnecessarily disrupting established protection.

The proposed allocation represents licensing credits, not a cash grant. The initiative will be introduced in phases, with detailed eligibility criteria, credit allocation and redemption terms, partner participation options, and service availability to be communicated as the program is rolled out.

2. Forward-deployed engineers to turn technology into stronger defenses

Recognizing that cybersecurity modernization requires more than technology alone, TrendAI™ plans to mobilize forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) and technical specialists to work directly with participating organizations.

These specialists will work alongside participating organizations and their existing partners, where appropriate, to assess critical exposures, identify security gaps, prioritize risk reduction and accelerate the deployment of modern security capabilities.

FDE engagements will initially prioritize organizations whose security is particularly important to national infrastructure, economic activity and interconnected supply chains. For smaller organizations, Trend Micro intends to work through appropriate delivery models and its partner ecosystem to help extend the initiative's reach.

3. Expert-led detection, response and operational resilience

Through TrendAI™'s MDR capabilities and security expertise, eligible organizations will be able to explore additional support for continuous threat monitoring, incident investigation and response.

The initiative aims to help organizations move beyond isolated security controls toward a coordinated approach that connects exposure management, threat detection, incident response and proactive risk reduction.

Trend Micro also protects more than 10 million consumers across Japan through its TrendLife™ business unit. Through local partners and a network of managed service provider (MSP) partners serving over 230,000 small and medium-sized businesses, we also help protect close to 2 million business devices. Building on this foundation, we will continue to help strengthen security for consumers and small businesses alike.

4. 60-day free trial of Worry-Free Business Security Services provided (TBD)

Small and medium-sized businesses play a vital role in supply chains, and strengthening their security is increasingly urgent. For these customers, a 60-day free trial of Worry-Free Business Security Services will be provided. In addition, TrendLife™ is considering new support for the Worry-Free series together with its channel partners. Further details will be announced as they are finalized. Note: The free trial is available only to new customers in Japan and must be started by December 31, 2026.

5. Exploring AI-Powered Scam Protection to Strengthen Digital Trust on LINE

As small businesses increasingly rely on LINE Official Accounts (LINE OA) to engage with customers, everyday interactions may also expose them to scams disguised as customer inquiries, suspicious links, or fraudulent requests.

TrendLife™ is advancing API integrations with providers of LINE-related services, enabling AI-powered scam detection capabilities to be seamlessly embedded into customer touchpoints and helping strengthen protection for both businesses and their customers. We are currently working with partners, including Crescendo Lab, one of Asia's leading LINE CRM providers, and are in the final stages of preparation for commercial deployment by the end of the year.

＜For consumers＞

6. 90 days of Trend Micro ScamCheck provided free of charge

TrendLife™ will provide 90 days of complimentary access to Trend Micro ScamCheck, our mobile scam protection app. In the event that leaked personal information is misused in phone, email, or other scam attempts, Trend Micro ScamCheck helps protect users from potential scams.

The benefit will be provided through the following channels:

TrendLife Online Store: Customers who purchase through the site below will have their subscription extended by 90 days. https://shop.trendlife.com/ja-jp/products/scam-buster.asp

App stores: Please follow the instructions on the page below. https://trendlife.com/ja-jp/blog/news-tmsc-3-month-free-trial/

Note: In all cases, customers must start using the service by December 31, 2026. This offer is available only to customers in Japan.

A lasting commitment to Japan's cyber resilience

Trend Micro will work with customers and partners to translate this initiative into measurable improvements in cybersecurity, with plans to track participation, modernization progress and defensive outcomes.

Organizations and partners interested in participating can contact their Trend Micro representative or visit the Initiative Landing Page to register their interest and receive updates as program details and participation opportunities become available. For individual customers, please contact us through TrendLife™ website.

About Trend Micro

Trend Micro Incorporated is a Japan-headquartered global cybersecurity company dedicated to protecting the digital world. Drawing on decades of security expertise, worldwide threat intelligence and cybersecurity innovation, the company helps organizations and individuals protect their digital environments and build resilience against evolving cyber threats.

For more information, visit trendmicro.com or TrendLife™ (Japanese).
